scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: Duplicate captures observed on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 with counts 118 and 124 respectively.

F-06.statement: PSP logs show 242 duplicate orders in 2026-09-09..10, all as gateway timeout retries without idempotency keys; earlier period had 0 duplicate orders despite 238 timeout retries that were deduplicated when idempotency keys were present.

F-07.statement: SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on 2026-09-09 (temporary latency debugging, no rollback).

F-08.statement: Four orders (O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318) each have two captures and are not refunded.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The requester's framing is correct: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

H-ROOT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN.statement: The operational root cause differs from the requested solution and must be established from data

interpretation_history.interpretation: Duplicate captures appear on Sep 9-10, correlating with high gateway timeout retries, indicating that timeout-induced retries may cause double charges.
The weekly double-charge ticket count shows a sharp increase in weeks 2026-W37 and W38, indicating the double-charge problem is worsening recently.

In Sep 9-10, all duplicate capture events (242) were gateway timeout retries that lacked idempotency keys, while earlier period showed timeout retries were deduplicated when idempotency keys were used.

The audit log shows SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging, which aligns with the observed duplicate captures caused by timeout retries lacking idempotency keys on Sep 9-10.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that idempotency-key enforcement was deliberately turned off on 2026-09-09 for latency debugging and was intended to be temporary, with runtime confirmation required to turn it back on.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports that customers are furious about double charges and demands faster, nicer apology replies. This indicates that the perceived problem is customer dissatisfaction with the current response, not necessarily the underlying charge duplication.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook states that re-enabling idempotency_key_enforcement via the set_capture_idempotency operation requires runtime confirmation by the payments operations manager (SH-OPS) and is reversible.

U-01.question: Will restoring idempotency_key_enforcement increase gateway timeout errors or latency, harming checkout success?
U-01.decision_impact: May require fallback or latency mitigation before full rollout.
U-01.resolution_path: Run a canary test: enable idempotency_key_enforcement on a small traffic slice, monitor gateway timeout rates and capture latency for 24 h before broader rollout.
U-01.safe_placeholder: Keep enforcement off but increase manual review of duplicate captures and continue issuing apology replies via the existing CS process.

U-02.question: Are there any additional root causes of duplicate captures besides missing idempotency keys (e.g., PSP‑side retries)?
U-02.decision_impact: If other causes exist, fixing the gateway setting alone will not eliminate all duplicates.
U-02.resolution_path: After re‑enabling the setting, analyze PSP logs for duplicate orders that still have an idempotency key present; investigate any remaining duplicates.
U-02.safe_placeholder: Continue to alert on any duplicate capture regardless of cause and maintain the existing apology‑reply workflow.

A-01.statement: PSP deduplication depends solely on the presence of an idempotency key on the capture retry; no other factors affect deduplication.

A-02.statement: Re‑enabling idempotency_key_enforcement will restore deduplication without adversely affecting capture latency or gateway timeout rates.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice
problem_definition.root_problem: Disabling idempotency_key_enforcement on the payment gateway causes gateway timeout retries to be resent without idempotency keys, which the PSP does not deduplicate, resulting in duplicate captures and double charges.

trace.summary: The configuration change is a simple gateway operation requiring only runtime confirmation by SH‑OPS (E‑07, K‑GW). No complex logic or learning is needed; an agent could only be used for optional latency monitoring after the change.

structural_remedies.description: Re-enable idempotency_key_enforcement on the payment gateway via the set_capture_idempotency operation, requiring runtime confirmation by the payments operations manager (SH-OPS).
structural_remedies.rationale: Changing a gateway configuration is a quick operation; the remaining contest time is 150 minutes (budget_remaining_minutes 225, minute 75).; residual gap: Potential increase in gateway timeout errors or latency remains unknown (U-01). Still need to verify that re-enabling enforcement does not harm checkout success (unknown U-01). Why agent needed: No agent is required for the configuration change itself; only runtime confirmation by SH-OPS is needed, which is a human approval step already captured in constraint K-GW. An agent could be used to monitor latency after the change, but it is not strictly required to remove the root cause.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement on 2026-09-09 (E-04, E-05). → Gateway timeout retries continue at the usual rate (E-01 shows ~118‑124 retries per day). → Without idempotency keys, timeout retries are sent to the PSP lacking the key (E-03 shows second capture sent without idempotency key). → The PSP does not deduplicate retries missing the key, creating a duplicate capture (E-03 shows all 242 duplicate orders are timeout retries without idempotency key). → Duplicate captures generate double‑charge support tickets (E-02 shows a spike in double_charge_tickets). → Customers experience double charges and complain (E-06 stakeholder claim).; rejected framings: [('H-REQUESTER-FRAMING', 'Evidence shows duplicate charges stem from missing idempotency keys on timeout retries, not from lack of apology replies; building an AI assistant addresses the symptom only and does not prevent the root cause.')]

proposal.summary: Disabling idempotency_key_enforcement on the payment gateway causes gateway timeout retries to be resent without idempotency keys, which the PSP does not deduplicate, resulting in duplicate captures and double charges.[E-01][E-02][E-03][E-04][E-05] Duplicate captures spiked on Sep 9‑10 (118 and 124 per day) correlating with high gateway timeout retries,[E-01] while double‑charge tickets rose from 9/11 to 288/301 per week,[E-02] and PSP logs show all duplicate orders were gateway timeout retries lacking idempotency keys whereas earlier periods with keys had zero duplicates.[E-03] The gateway audit log records SH‑PAY disabling idempotency_key_enforcement on 2026‑09‑09 for latency debugging,[E-04] and the stakeholder confirms this was a temporary change requiring runtime confirmation to restore.[E-05] The release provides the duplicate capture monitoring feature—a query to fetch open duplicate capture orders and ongoing monitoring of payments‑db—as specified in the solution design and plan.[SD-1][W-WI-1][W-WI-2] The DEFINE gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS due to the high‑criticality unknown U‑01 (whether restoring idempotency_key_enforcement will increase gateway timeout errors or latency) which was deferred to VOB‑U‑01; because the unknown lies outside the release scope and the gate conditionally passed, the release proceeds with known limitations.[U-01][VOB-U-01] Known limitations: DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs (linked to unknown U‑01 and VOB‑U‑01).[U-01][VOB-U-01]; VOB‑U‑01 remains open, representing a blocking scope outside the release.[VOB-U-01]; Any residual duplicate capture rate after the fix will be documented as a known limitation (as stated in the release limitations).
key_points: Problem: disabling idempotency key enforcement → duplicate captures & double charges.
Established by: E-01, E-02, E-03, E-04, E-05.
Released: duplicate capture monitoring (SD-1, W-WI-1, W-WI-2).
Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION due to conditional pass and unknown U-01/VOB-U-01.
Limitations: gate conditional pass, VOB-U-01 open, residual duplicate capture rate documented.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate resulted in a conditional pass, deferring the high‑criticality unknown U‑01 (gateway timeout/latency impact) to VOB‑U‑01.
VOB‑U‑01 remains open, meaning the blocking scope (set_capture_idempotency on gateway‑config) is outside the current release.
Any remaining duplicate capture rate after the fix will be recorded as a known limitation.
